exposure: Doppler parameters (Absent or reversed end-diastolic velocity in the umbilical artery and ductus venosus)
outcome: Cranial ultrasound abnormalities (including periventricular leukomalacia, intraventricular hemorrhage, and basal ganglia lesions)
cohort: The study participants included 83 delivered fetuses with intrauterine growth restriction and 75 gestational age-matched control fetuses born between 28-34 weeks of gestation.
finding: Gestational age at birth and absent or reversed end-diastolic velocity in the umbilical artery and ductus venosus within 1 week before childbirth were reliable predictors of cranial ultrasound abnormalities during the neonatal period, and the incidence of CUAs and neonatal mortality was significantly higher in IUGR fetuses.
